THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 08.04.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA. No.1023/2016  3  2025:KER:32670  JUDGMENT Dated this the 8th day of April, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.1014/2008 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Palakkad is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience,
the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 22.6.2008.

According to the petitioner, on 22.6.2008 at about 11a.m., while he was riding pillion on a motor cycle, a jeep belonging to the 1 st respondent and driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down and as a result of which he sustained injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the K. Radhakrishnan vs Secretary, Grama Panchayat Kavassery on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121082129/
2 negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
2025:KER:32670 4.

sentences.text: The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A12.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,13,503/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri.V.A. Johnson Varikkappaalllil, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri. Lal K, Joseph, the learned 2025:KER:32670 Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working abroad earning Rs.25,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.3,500/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.
11. Before the Tribunal, the petitioner has not produced any documents to prove that he was employed abroad.
However, before this Court, he has produced the original passport, which will go to show that he was employed abroad since long back.
The last endorsement present in the passport shows that on 17.5.2008, he returned to Cohcin.

The accident occurred in this case on 22.6.2008,
about one month and five days after his arrival at Cochin.
Therefore, from the above passport, it can be seen that he was working abroad and the accident occurred while 2025:KER:32670 he came home on leave.

12. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2008 will come to Rs.6,500/-.

3 Rs.7,500/-.

sentences.text:
In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"avulsion fracture of PCL right tibia."
He was treated as inpatient for a period of 20 days and in the meantime, he had undergone a surgery also.
14. As per Exhibit A12 disability certificate issued by PW1, the petitioner suffered 19% permanent physical disability.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as such and hence, I do not find any grounds to interfere with the same.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted as 19%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 49 years.

Therefore, 25% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 13, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.2,77,875/-.
16. Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.10,500/- being the income for 3 months @ Rs.3,500/-.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 6 months.

Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.45,000/-
(7,500x 6 months).
17. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.9,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.25,000/- and towards bystander expenses Rs.1,500/- were awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those 2025:KER:32670 heads are on the lower side.
Towards 'extra nourishment' no compensation was awarded.
18. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 10 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' and 'bystander expenses' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.40,000/-, Rs,25,000/- and Rs.2,000/- respectively.

Towards 'extra nourishment' petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.3,000/-.
19.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
